text:
Priya: Hit a fragmentation cliff on r5-gpu when validating NUMA staging. Lots of tiny frees/allocs (~1-16KB) across domains; free lists explode and p99 spikes.

Dan: Can you paste the minimal pattern?

Priya: microbatch workload: many ephemeral ~4KB tensors, threads pinned to different NUMA zones, allocator uses first-fit freelist per-slab so freed runs are non-local.

Jules: Sounds like freelist hotspotting. Long-term we could do slab-splitting or a bitmap fastpath for tiny allocs. Bitmap gives O(1) find but needs atomics.

Marco: Hybrid bitmap+freelist could be good: bitmap for fixed 4KB subpages, freelist for larger/coalesced blocks. Fallback path keeps correctness.

Priya: Proposed flow: tiny alloc (<8KB) -> try bitmap_alloc(local_zone); if fail -> zone freelist; free mirrors that. No coalescing in bitmap domain.

Dan: Concurrency: per-word atomics (64-bit) for bitmap ops, avoid locks. We accept some internal fragmentation to keep latency low.

Jules: Telemetry: tiny_alloc_local_hit_ratio, bitmap_alloc_latency_p99, remote_bitmap_penalty_count. Also emit bitmap_density for background compaction triggers.

Marco: Metadata budget: 1 bit per 4KB subpage -> ~32KB per 1GB slab; acceptable. For migration snapshot store the bitmap as part of residency data.

Priya: Rollout: feature flag tiny_bitmap_alloc=true on one NUMA node class, non-coalescing mode, quota tenants. infra-bot can create canary.

infra-bot: Canary created -> id=canary-1715006795 target=r5-gpu-numaA cfg={"tiny_bitmap_alloc":true,"bitmap_subpage_size":4096}

Dan: Tests: racey alloc/free unit tests, stress harness with 1k RPS microbatches. Metrics: p99 alloc latency, local_hit_ratio, resident_frag_ratio.

Jules: Edge case: internal fragmentation could exceed threshold. Plan a background scanner that converts long free runs into freelist blocks when density drops; throttled by SLO.

Marco: Owners: Priya prototype, Jules API+telemetry, Marco infra/canary. Priya aim for prototype PR by next Tue.

Priya: Will drop the link to the PR and ping for review once ready.

Dan: :eyes:
